Pixel Weather’s new feature lets you report your local conditions now

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Default weather apps are notoriously unreliable, but Google is giving owners a chance to help improve things.
  • A recent revision to the Pixel Weather app introduced a fresh “Report current weather” card.
  • “Share the current weather condition,” the card says, “to improve local forecasts.” If you tap it, you’re given options to indicate whether the current temperature is accurate, warmer, or colder than the app says, and what your current conditions are, with options like cloudy, clear, rain showers, strong thunderstorms, and rain showers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Default weather apps are notoriously unreliable, but Google is giving owners a chance to help improve things.

A recent revision to the Pixel Weather app introduced a fresh “Report current weather” card. If the weather you’re experiencing doesn’t match what the app is saying, you can report the discrepancy.

“Share the current weather condition,” the card says, “to improve local forecasts.” If you tap it, you’re given options to indicate whether the current temperature is accurate, warmer, or colder than the app says, and what your current conditions are, with options like cloudy, clear, rain showers, strong thunderstorms, and rain showers.

According to recent reports, the card also indicates what the app currently thinks is happening for you to use as the basis for your report. To find the card, scroll all the way to the bottom of your Pixel Weather app.

Also: Your best Google weather app alternatives (and what I recommend instead).

In a recent development, google mentioned that it will use your feedback, device location, and “some diagnostic information” to help improve forecasts. Nothing you report will be associated with your Google account. The app doesn’t explain exactly how Google uses your reports, but I’ve reached out to see if the company can offer any details.

According to recent reports, as someone who doesn’t put a ton of faith into default weather apps, I see this as a step in the right direction toward regaining some trust. Even if it’s not yet clear how Google will use the information you send, the goal of improving forecasts is an key one.

Also: I switched to MyRadar as my main Android Auto weather app and don’t regret it.

A large part of what makes weather apps unreliable is that they lack human insight, and a computer usually can’t grasp the nuance of a local forecast the way a meteorologist would. Experts have also warned of reduced weather forecast accuracy due to recent NOAA budget cuts.

According to recent reports, the Apple Weather app has a similar feature, so it’s good to see Google catch up. I couldn’t find a feature like this for Samsung or any other native app. One of the most popular third-party apps, Weather Underground, does feature a “Report your local weather” prompt. It also gathers information from hundreds of thousands of connected home weather stations.

This latest Pixel Weather feature was present on three Pixel phones in my home, so the rollout appears to be widespread.

Dell Just Reported Earnings and Raised Its Forecast by $10 Billion. Is the Stock a Buy After Tuesday's Selloff?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, dell Technologies (DELL -11.83%) shares rose about 3% to $305 in after-hours trading Tuesday after the manufacturer reported that quarterly revenue more than doubled and raised its full-year forecast.
  • In a recent development, hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE -16.31%) led that decline.
  • It has been revealed that dell's earnings release for the quarter ended Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:54PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Dell Technologies ›.

According to recent reports, dell Technologies (DELL -11.83%) shares rose about 3% to $305 in after-hours trading Tuesday after the manufacturer reported that quarterly revenue more than doubled and raised its full-year forecast. The stock had closed at $295.28 in the regular session, down 12% from Monday's $334.91, as AI hardware shares sold off.

In a recent development, hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE -16.31%) led that decline. Its shares fell about 16% after executives said on Monday's earnings call that memory and other components could stay scarce through at least the second half of 2028. HPE also guided for its cloud and AI business to keep about 14% of sales as operating profit in fiscal 2027, down from 18.4% in the quarter it just reported. Dell, which sells many of the same servers, fell with it.

It has been revealed that dell's earnings release for the quarter ended Oct. 30 showed revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. And adjusted earnings rose 265% to $9.45 per share, well above the $6.59 analysts expected.

Recent findings suggest that most of the growth came from the Infrastructure Solutions Group, which sells servers, networking, and storage. Its revenue tripled to $42.0 billion. AI-optimized server sales rose 291% to $22.0 billion, and traditional servers and networking rose 235% to $15.0 billion. "We are now a different company," Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke stated in the release.

Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI orders in the quarter and ended it with a record AI backlog of $132.3 billion, about two-thirds of the revenue it expects for the whole year.

According to recent reports, gross margin was 21% of revenue, up from 20.7% a year earlier. Helping to drive that increase, the infrastructure business kept 17% of its sales as operating profit, compared with 12.4% a year ago, and its operating income quadrupled to $7.1 billion.

Lower spending also helped. Operating expenses fell to 7.5% of revenue from 12.9%, and Chief Financial Officer David Kennedy mentioned that is driving "higher profitability, even as AI servers become a larger part of our business." AI servers tend to carry thinner margins than storage, so a rising AI share usually pulls margins down, but this quarter it clearly didn't.

It has been revealed that on the other hand, PCs were the weak spot. The Client Solutions Group grew revenue by 3% to $12.9 billion, consumer sales fell by 15%, and the segment's operating income slipped by 6% to $704 million.

It has been revealed that dell raised its full-year revenue forecast by $10 billion to $202 billion, up 78% from last year, and its AI server sales forecast to $78 billion from $74 billion. It now expects adjusted earnings of $29.68 per share, up from $25.50. For the fourth quarter, it guided revenue to $56.3 billion and adjusted earnings to $8.40 per share.

Separately, the organization returned a record $4.9 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends in the quarter, and its board approved an additional $25 billion in repurchases. Free cash flow rose to $3.5 billion from $506 million a year earlier.

Inventories rose to $29.4 billion on Oct. 30 from $10.4 billion at the end of January, and total debt rose to $37.7 billion from $31.5 billion. If component costs keep climbing, as HPE expects, Dell may need to keep raising prices, and one quarter of higher margins doesn't show it can do that indefinitely.

The stock is also volatile. It rose about 20% on Monday after Nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) reinstated CEO Jensen Huang, then gave back most of that gain on Tuesday.

Sources indicate that even after Tuesday's after-hours gain, the stock trades at about 10 times the adjusted earnings Dell expects for the fiscal year ending in January. That's a low multiple for a company whose revenue just doubled and whose backlog covers much of next year. And while the stock fell on worries about a rival's margins, Dell's own margins rose.

Industry observers note that the case depends on AI spending holding up, the same bet behind most AI stocks. Investors who already own plenty of semiconductor stocks and other AI infrastructure names should know Dell adds to that exposure rather than diversifying it. Those who want to see whether component costs hit margins can wait for next quarter's report.

You won’t see a Galaxy Watch 10 until 2028 – here’s why

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (345 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You might have to wait over a year to get the Samsung Galaxy Watch 10: Samsung will not release any fresh Galaxy smartwatch in 2027, South Korea’s ET News reported on Sunday.
  • In a recent development, in an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News.
  • I am not mad at this decision by Samsung.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You might have to wait over a year to get the Samsung Galaxy Watch 10: Samsung will not release any fresh Galaxy smartwatch in 2027, South Korea’s ET News reported on Sunday.

In a recent development, in an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News. The switch follows other cost-cutting measures that will reduce production of the tech giant’s midrange smartphone lineup while increasing its premium Galaxy S27 offerings.

I am not mad at this decision by Samsung. Annual smartwatch updates are usually iterative anyway. Take Apple, for example. Its Apple Watch Series 10, released in 2024, had the same chip as the Apple Watch Series 11, released a year later. The most recent Apple Watch, the Apple Watch Series 12, has the same battery life as the Apple Watch Series 11. I’d expect Apple to keep its latest sensors, which debuted on the Series 12 and Ultra 4, for its Series 13 or Ultra 5 next year.

Samsung’s Galaxy Watch 9, which debuted with a different chip and added a few more hours of battery, had the same bones as the Galaxy Watch 8.

If some of the biggest features on these smartwatches remain the same for a few years, why not change the release schedule to a biannual one?

Recent findings suggest that also: Galaxy Watch 9 vs. Galaxy Watch 8: I’ve compared both models, here’s my advice.

Some of the most substantial updates that arrive on latest devices like the Galaxy Watch 9 or Apple Watch Series 12 normally arrive through software updates, which end up landing on previous watch generations upon launch as well.

By switching from an annual release cycle to a biannual one, Samsung could drum up more excitement and anticipation between launches, and be able to surprise its customers with more purchase-worthy updates.

Samsung did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

With a higher-tier Game Pass Ultimate subscription ($23 per month), you can access hundreds of titles, including new ones on release day.

Here’s everything Microsoft is adding to Xbox Game Pass soon.

In a recent development, new to Game Pass Premium. Previously added to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

This sequel to the 2022 first-person shooter High on Life has players once again traveling throughout space and taking down bad guys with the help of an arsenal of talking guns. The game comes from Squanch Games, which was founded by a co-creator of the Rick and Morty series, so expect some raunchy humor and antics.

To survive, you have to fight and evade other test subjects in a massive facility run by the shady Murkoff Corporation.

You’ll solve puzzles, explore landscapes inspired by Northern Sweden and take in a heartwarming story told via fuzzy friends.

While Microsoft is adding several games to Game Pass, it’s also removing eight others on Nov. 30. So you still have some time to complete your main campaign or any side quests before you’ll have to buy these games separately.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure manufacturer Oracle (ORCL) recently revealed better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

After hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he stated.

In a recent development, "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," remarked DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

Industry observers note that while Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as upcoming contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

Sources indicate that diFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

"RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," said Gesuale.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space company with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst stated, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

Gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

"Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," said Anmuth.

Sources indicate that in the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst remarked. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst mentioned. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

Anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

PennantPark (PNNT -5.94%) reported fourth quarter core net investment income of $0.13 per share and a portfolio value of $1.2 billion. Management stated that the portfolio is positioned to take advantage of the current interest rate environment and indicated a focus on rotating equity co-investments into income-generating debt assets. The company reported that its government services and defense investments remain a high-conviction sector due to durable federal funding and resilient cash flow profiles.

It has been revealed that as of September 30th, our portfolio totaled $1.2 billion, and during the quarter, we continued to originate attractive investment opportunities and invested a total of $75 million at a weighted average yield of 9.4%, including $25 million invested into five new platform investments with a median debt-to-EBITDA of 4.8 times, interest coverage of 2.2 times, and a loan-to-value ratio of 36%. We added two investments to non-accrual status and removed one investment, and ended the quarter with five non-accrual investments out of a diversified pool of 160 companies, representing 2.1% of the portfolio at cost and 0.6% at market value. Our PSLF joint venture portfolio continues to be a significant contributor to our core net investment income.

On a last 12 months basis, PNNT's average cash yield on invested capital in the JV was 14.7%. As of September 30th, the JV portfolio totaled $1.2 billion. In July, the JV refinanced the AAA tranches of its $300 million debt securitization, reducing the securitization's weighted average spread by 97 basis points to 1.69% from 2.66%. We expect the JV to continue to be a significant contributor to PNNT's NII in future quarters. Turning to portfolio positioning, I'd like to highlight our government services and defense investments. Government services and defense remains one of our highest conviction sectors and has historically been among our best performing investment areas.

According to recent reports, we remain highly constructive on the long-term outlook for government services and defense because the sector possesses several characteristics that align well with our investment philosophy. Demand has historically been supported by durable federal funding priorities and long-term contracts that provide meaningful revenue visibility and stability. Many of these businesses exhibit resilient cash flow profiles, variable cost structures, and are generally less sensitive to broader economic cycles than many commercial industries. In addition, the sector continues to benefit from active M&A markets and strong valuation support, thereby providing multiple avenues for value creation. One example of this is Echelon InvestCo.

In a recent development, through our equity co-investment in Echelon InvestCo, we have an ongoing equity investment in a fast-growing defense tech company, Shield AI. Shield AI recently announced an acquisition and a capital raise at an indicative valuation for investment of $2.6 million above the value on September 30th of $2 million. This increase equates to $0.04 per share. Within the government services and defense portfolio, our investments are focused on businesses that support the Department of War and other mission-critical government agencies. We focus on companies addressing high-priority national security initiatives, including modernization of defense systems and digital infrastructure, cyber and electronic warfare capabilities, modeling and simulation, counter-drone technologies, and next-generation autonomous systems.

Recent findings suggest that we believe these priorities will remain central to U.S. defense spending for years to come, creating a favorable backdrop for continued investment opportunities. On a combined basis, including the joint venture portfolio, government services and defense represents approximately 12.4% of total investments. Given our experience, sourcing capabilities, and the attractive opportunity set, we intend to increase that exposure over time. Another highlight of our portfolio is AKW, a U.K. provider of adapted bathroom and kitchen products that help elderly and disabled individuals live independently at home. Since taking control of AKW in 2018, we have strengthened management, improved operations, and invested in growth.

Sources indicate that on October 27, 2026, AKW acquired Mobility Bathing Group, entering the private pay market and creating cross-selling, marketing, and cost-saving opportunities. We are targeting an exit of the investment in AKW in the next 18 to 24 months. As of September 30, we held $48 million of the first lien term loan, marked at par, and common equity valued at $77.7 million against a cost of $5.9 million. Turning to software, our exposure represents approximately 3.1% of the portfolio. These investments follow our core middle market strategy and consist of cash pay loans with financial covenants, moderate leverage, and relatively short durations. These businesses provide mission-critical enterprise software to regulated industries, including defense, healthcare, and financial services.

Let me now turn to the broader market environment. M&A activity has increased recently, although overall conditions remain uneven. Private equity sponsors remain active, and we are seeing a growing pipeline of attractive opportunities across both new originations as well as add-on investments. We are optimistic that activity levels will remain strong throughout the end of the year and into next year. We expect increased transaction activity to drive repayments across the portfolio, including opportunities to monetize equity co-investments and to redeploy that capital into income-generating investments. In the core middle market, the pricing for high-quality first lien term loans remains attractive, typically ranging from SOFR plus 500 to 550 basis points, with leverage of approximately 4.5x EBITDA.

Importantly, these structures continue to include meaningful covenant protections, which is in contrast to the covenant-light structures prevalent in the upper middle market. We believe the current environment favors lenders with established private equity sponsor relationships, consistent access to deal flow, and disciplined underwriting. These are longstanding strengths of the PennantPark platform. We continue to believe that the core middle market offers an attractive risk-adjusted opportunity. Companies in this segment generally have EBITDA of $10 million-$50 million and often operate below the practical threshold of the broadly syndicated loan and high-yield markets.

As a result, lenders can typically conduct extensive diligence, negotiate meaningful financial covenants, structure transactions with appropriate leverage and equity cushions, and maintain regular access to tech giant financial information. Since our inception nearly 19 years ago, PNNT has invested $9.9 billion at an average yield of 11.1%, while maintaining a loss ratio on invested capital of roughly 20 basis points annually, a testament to our consistent and disciplined approach through multiple market cycles. As a provider of strategic capital who fuels the growth of our portfolio companies, in many cases, we participate in the upside of that company by making an equity co-investment. Our returns on these equity co-investments have been excellent over time.

According to recent reports, overall, for our platform from inception through September 30th, we have invested over $635 million in these equity co-investments and have generated an IRR of 25% and a multiple on invested capital of 2x. Looking ahead, our experienced team and broad origination platform position us well to generate attractive deal flow. We remain steadfast in our commitment to capital preservation and maintaining a disciplined, patient investment approach. We continue to focus on investing in high-quality middle market companies with strong free cash flow generation. We capture that value through first lien senior secured loans, and we pay out those cash flows in the form of dividends to our shareholders.

CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Packages Could Be at Risk of Holiday Porch Theft

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Major holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a plan to protect your package from porch pirates.
  • CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts.
  • But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a big risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Major holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a plan to protect your package from porch pirates.

CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts. This year, the average package value is $276.24, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees.

But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a big risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered. On the other hand, some bad actors don’t seem to mind being caught in the act on home security cameras, so are they really enough to deter bad actors? And what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

According to recent reports, CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera.

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

It has been revealed that “Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other issues like break-ins,” said CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”.

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma said that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and fresh porch theft tactics are always on the horizon.

In a recent development, there are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival.

In a recent development, so while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to proposal how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

Online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults strategy to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06.

By generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

Lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages.

Recent findings suggest that “I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” noted Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931.

Thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk.

Among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%).

But personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively).

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

According to recent reports, you shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery.

Recent findings suggest that “Delivery boxes have reached a new level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” remarked Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”.

If you don’t want to install a newly introduced security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers.

According to recent reports, home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft.

There are two deterrents that are keeping US adults from having security devices — cost and privacy. Findings show that 20% of US adults lack home security measures due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. That’s followed by 9% who don’t want to use cameras because of privacy concerns.

Industry observers note that “Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” said Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.”.

If you’re looking for a camera that’s off-the-grid, consider the Arlo Go 2. It’s an LTE camera, so it uses a cellular data connection instead of Wi-Fi. It still finds a signal, supports app operation and live video viewing. If you’re looking for a power-over-Ethernet camera that uses a cable connection, the Reolink Duo 3 is a good choice.

Sources indicate that lacoma added that many companies also offer ways to use local video storage and local AI detection so nothing is stored in the cloud. There are also features, such as customizable privacy zones, to minimize privacy concerns when used with the right precautions.

Among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription.

Sources indicate that those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it.

Sources indicate that but that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or newly introduced security devices, make a proposal to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays.

Recent findings suggest that “Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” stated Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. Latest practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”.

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • With Claude Ship, declared in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

With Claude Ship, declared in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

Industry observers note that “Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

According to recent reports, the new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise looks. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic noted, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic said.

According to recent reports, “It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic remarked it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic mentioned in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz mentioned the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

It has been revealed that also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

Recent findings suggest that “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he mentioned. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz stated he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the organization and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he said.

Developer platforms overall are adapting to the fresh state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

According to recent reports, individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “owners won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Still, that depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the latest PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

In a recent development, anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.

Recent findings suggest that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points higher than yesterday and four basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

In a recent development, recently news about big tech has often pulled rates down. Investor concerns about AI profitability keep cropping up, and when they do, tech stocks and bonds lose their appeal and Treasuries have been picking up the slack. Mortgage rates are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury, and Treasury prices and yields move inversely. More demand for the 10YT drives prices up, and sends yields (and thus, mortgage rates) down.

Recent findings suggest that today's the opposite, though. Investors are having a bout of tech exuberance as Jensen Huang got reinstated as Nvidia CEO, and lots of excitement about tech stocks and bonds means less enthusiasm for Treasuries.

Recent findings suggest that here's the thing, though: Markets are fickle. They also move fast. And they aren't the only influence on mortgage rates.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

It has been revealed that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to fresh inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Industry observers note that lately, we've seen two narratives influencing mortgage rates battling it out; depending on which one's stronger, daily rates move higher or lower. Up top I talked about how shifting perceptions of big tech have been driving mortgage rates (and yes, today, pushing them higher, though usually it's pulled rates down.) When rates are moving higher, more often it's been thanks to inflation — and while it's a lightweight work week, we're about to get heavyweight inflation news.

Industry observers note that the latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely.

Recent findings suggest that the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation, so you can guess how things are likely to go at the Fed's December meeting. Markets already feel fairly certain about a quarter-percent rate hike.

Sources indicate that we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three major inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI showed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

According to recent reports, predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out Wednesday morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

And speaking of: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. Wall Street's $1.4 Trillion Bubble May Be on the Verge of Bursting -- but It's Not Artificial Intelligence (AI)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the past four years, euphoria for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has fueled a historic rally in the stock market.
  • In a recent development, although much of Wall Street's attention is focused on whether AI stocks are overvalued, another vulnerability is lurking in the background.
  • Let's explore why margin debt represents one of Wall Street's biggest threats and what smart investors can do about it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adam Spatacco – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

Over the past four years, euphoria for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has fueled a historic rally in the stock market. Enthusiasm surrounding AI infrastructure and software has helped propel the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.50%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -1.48%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.85%) to record highs.

In a recent development, although much of Wall Street's attention is focused on whether AI stocks are overvalued, another vulnerability is lurking in the background. Investors are borrowing unprecedented sums of money to participate in the stock market's ongoing rally. This introduces another layer of risk into an already frothy market.

Let's explore why margin debt represents one of Wall Street's biggest threats and what smart investors can do about it.

Industry observers note that margin debt is a financial term used to describe money investors borrow from a brokerage firm to buy stocks. This practice is more commonly known as leverage. It allows investors to increase their purchasing power without committing an equivalent amount of their own capital up front.

In a recent development, although borrowing can be lucrative when stocks are rising, leverage works in both directions. For example, imagine you have $10,000 and borrow another $10,000 from a brokerage firm. With $20,000 invested, a 25% increase in the portfolio's value generates a $5,000 gain. This represents a 50% return on your original capital. However, if the portfolio declines by 25%, you would lose $5,000, or half of your original investment. A 50% decline effectively wipes out your original capital.

According to data compiled by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), margin debt reached a record $1.5 trillion in June. To appreciate the magnitude of that figure, let's take a look at borrowing levels during other periods of unusually high speculation in the stock market.

Industry observers note that although today's borrowing levels dwarf the historical figures in terms of absolute dollars, it's notable to consider the fact that the stock market has become considerably larger. Nevertheless, the rapid accumulation of debt over the last year or so suggests investors are developing more of an appetite for risk.

One of the most dangerous aspects of using leverage is that investors do not necessarily control when their positions are sold. Brokerage firms require investors to maintain a minimum level of liquidity in their margin accounts. If declining stock prices cause an account to fall below that threshold, investors could face a margin call. This would require them to deposit additional collateral or reduce their positions.

Brokerages also have the authority to liquidate positions without obtaining an investor's permission. When this happens across several accounts at the same time, the forced selling puts additional downward pressure on stock prices. As a result, more margin calls are triggered, and a destructive cycle is created.

With all of that stated, current margin debt levels could suggest investors are moderating their risk exposure. At the end of October, margin debt was recorded at $1.4 trillion, or about 3.6% below its peak from June. While this could indicate investors are becoming more cautious, declining balances can also reflect forced liquidations rather than voluntary reductions in risk.

It's important to understand that elevated margin debt doesn't necessarily mean a stock market crash is imminent. Borrowing often increases alongside rising stock prices. Ultimately, margin debt is better viewed as a potential amplifier of market volatility rather than a reliable predictor of when a crash or drawdown will occur.

It has been revealed that even if excessive leverage contributes to a pullback, smart investors should remember that the stock market always demonstrates resilience. The S&P 500 declined by 49% following the dot-com bubble and nearly 57% during the financial crisis. More recently, the index fell 34% during the COVID-19 crash and 25% during the 2022 bear market. Despite these setbacks -- depicted by the grey columns in the chart below -- the S&P 500 eventually recovered and reached new record highs.

The takeaway here is that investors who buy stocks using their own capital wind up having more financial flexibility to endure prolonged downturns than those whose brokerage firms can force them to sell at unfavorable prices.

Although nobody knows whether today's borrowing levels will culminate in another stock market bubble bursting event, history suggests that staying diversified and remaining invested through volatility is a more prudent approach to building long-term wealth than attempting to predict the next market crash.

Netflix's economic moat comes from its scale. With more than 325 million paid memberships, it spreads its content budget across a far bigger audience than any rival can. Walt Disney's (DIS +1.86%) non-sports streaming segment, which includes Disney+ and Hulu, posted an 11.5% margin in its latest fiscal year.

Free cash flow is also expected to reach roughly $12 billion in 2026, compared to $9.5 billion last year. Growth is translating into serious profits.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

Engagement is a worry, too. View hours rose only 2% in the first half of 2026. Investors also didn't like management's decision to report that figure once a year, starting in 2027, instead of twice.

Sources indicate that but all this pessimism has reset the valuation. The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is now 15.1. That's cheaper than the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.50%). Shareholders aren't used to seeing Netflix shares on the discount rack.

At this multiple, Netflix looks like an interesting buy with $1,000. Just don't expect a smooth ride. The stock could move with heightened volatility in the near term. That's why patience is critical.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on Tuesday, Bambu Lab took the wraps off its third-generation 3D printer, the P3C. It brings to the mainstream the company’s “tool changer” technology, which was previously reserved for higher-end, flagship models like the $2,500 H3C. Given the P3C costs less than half the bigger model, it might be the perfect gift to get your favorite 3D printing hobbyist for Black Friday.

Recent findings suggest that the big deal here is the introduction of the Swaptek 7-tool changer, which allows you to switch to a different color or material in just 6 seconds, preventing you from having to stop and clean the nozzle every time. The technology produces significantly less waste and allows you to create faster prints.

Industry observers note that the tool changer technology also allows you to mix different materials with less of a fuss, so you can use a typical rigid plastic and something like a flexible rubber in a single pass without stopping. It can switch between different nozzle sizes in one job. You can switch between  0.2 mm, 0.4 mm, 0.6 mm and 0.8 mm midprint.

Sources indicate that the P3C ships with an integrated sealed AMS 3P filament management system that can store up to seven spools, each of which is on an independent feed path to the printer. You can also connect up to four external AMS units, supporting up to 22 colors.

The P3C is more than just a 3D printer. The Swaptek system supports interchangeable craft tools, letting you cut, draw or emboss on materials.

Bambu Lab also included a few features that make the P3C more approachable to newcomers. The P3C provides full-auto calibration, automatically aligning nozzle offsets and multi-tool heads so you don’t have to do it yourself. There’s also a built-in AI monitoring system that can detect issues like nozzle clogs and purge-bin jams early on. A new health management system will no longer spit out vague or obscure errors when something goes wrong. Instead, the new system will explain the issue in plain language and provide step-by-step troubleshooting right on the screen.

Sources indicate that CNET’s 3D printing expert, James Bricknell, hasn’t been able to test Bambu Labs’ latest model yet but is excited about it. “While the P3C didn’t arrive in time for a hands-on, it’s built with the same design language and hardware support as the recently released H3C. If it is anywhere near as good, and I think that’s likely, it’ll be at the top of any serious 3D printing enthusiast’s wish list.”.

The P3C 3D printer AMS combo is available now worldwide for $1,149. The combo includes the printer, AMS 3P as well as 5 0.4mm standard PrintTools. Two slots are left open for you to customize. This combo option comes with virtually everything you need to get started printing your works of art and more.

Stock markets remain volatile as investors weigh uncertainty in the Middle East, rising interest rates and concerns about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking a stable income stream can enhance their portfolios with the addition of dividend stocks. In this regard, tracking recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks that are backed by strong financials.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

According to recent reports, integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is the first dividend pick. Earlier this month, the manufacturer paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share. At an annualized dividend of $7.12 per share, CVX offers a dividend yield of about 3.5%.

After a meeting with senior leadership, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on CVX and raised his price target to $240 from $225. Among the key takeaways Mehta emphasized was that Chevron is building a solid pipeline of promising international exploration projects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean. In particular, he mentioned the focus on Venezuela, where Chevron expects to more than double gross production to 600 kbd from about 280 kbd by 2031, using three joint ventures.

Industry observers note that mehta also noted Chevron's efforts to deploy newly introduced technologies, especially in shale and tight-oil operations. CVX is focused on boosting productivity and efficiency to maximize free cash flow, he added.

Initiatives such as artificial lift optimization, AI and machine learning, and advanced chemical treatments are expected to improve recovery by about 10% in new wells. Consequently, capital spending per barrel in U.S. shale is projected to fall 25% in 2026, with total Permian spending dropping below $3.5 billion.

It has been revealed that mehta also said that Chevron sees power as a growth opportunity and is using its U.S. natural gas portfolio, key equipment and partnerships to meet rising demand. Notably, Chevron recently signed a 20-year power purchase deal with Microsoft (MSFT) to supply 2.67 GW of behind-the-meter capacity. This project, called Kilby, is expected to see its first power delivery in 2028 and generate mid-teens returns and long-term cash flows.

Mehta ranks No. 536 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 11.3%. See Chevron Statistics on TipRanks.

According to recent reports, enterprise Products Partners (EPD) is a master limited partnership (MLP) that provides midstream energy services to producers and consumers of natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals. With a quarterly cash distribution of 56 cents per common unit ($2.24 per common unit annualized), EPD offers a yield of about 6%.

In a recent development, following a recent call with the tech giant, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on EPD with a price target of $42. The analyst slightly lowered her estimates for the second half of 2026, citing margin and volume normalization, though demand dynamics remain strong.

Sources indicate that while the 5-star analyst expects a sequential decline due to normal seasonality and normalization following high spreads in the first half of the year, she still expects EPD to report another solid quarter (Q3 2026) and enter 2027 with a favorable setup. #108853. Industry News: A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

Industry News: A Human and an AI Model (Apparently) Solved the Riemann Hypothesis: What it Means for Future of Math

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2176 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems.
  • Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.
  • Industry observers note that “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Riemann Hypothesis is one of math’s oldest and most famous unsolved problems. It was originally put forward as a problem in 1859 by Bernhard Riemann, and professional and amateur mathematicians alike have made thousands of attempts to solve it. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge has apparently solved the problem with the help of AI, showing that in the battle of humans versus AI, the real winner might be both of them working together.

Alpöge made the announcement on Friday in a four-page document (PDF) on his personal web page.

Industry observers note that “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge said in the announcement. “In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too.”.

The actual hypothesis itself isn’t the biggest deal since all it does is make it easier to see the distribution of prime numbers. However, math didn’t come to a screeching halt just because the hypothesis hadn’t been proven. There are hundreds of other math theorems along with algorithms and cryptographic encryption methods that operate based on the assumption that the Riemann Hypothesis is true.

Sources indicate that the Riemann Hypothesis is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven Millennium Problems for this very reason. If Alpöge really did solve the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude’s help, it would remove a metaphorical logjam that’s been gumming up the works for over a century and a half. Most of those hundreds of math theorems would be proven as true overnight, and all of those algorithms and encryption methods would be validated. That would make solving the Riemann Hypothesis one of the greatest mathematical breakthroughs in history.

According to recent reports, “It is certainly an exciting time,” Paul Milewski, head of the department of mathematics at Penn State, mentioned in an email to CNET. “The Riemann Hypothesis (or any big theorem) is often not the ‘goal’ of mathematics. They are set up as grand challenges that require the development of newly introduced tools, new results along the way and new understanding. It is the ‘voyage’ and not the destination that matters the most.”.

As such, the mathematics community wasted no time testing the proof to see whether it was true. Two groups — Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative — independently verified the proof, with many other researchers running their own tests and coming to the same conclusion.

“We have full confidence that Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on the achievement,” the two groups said in a joint statement on Saturday.

This is certainly an exciting discovery, but it’s not without its obstacles. Alpöge’s proof was a staggering 250,000 pages of some of the most complex math ever written by a human or a machine. Alpöge provided 17 million lines of Lean code, a programming language specifically made for writing and checking proofs, and that’s how researchers were able to check the work and show it to be true.

The problem is that the average novel is about 300 pages, and that means that Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is approximately 833 novels’ worth of complex math. For reference, the longest work ever produced is World-2023, which holds the Guinness World Record at 100,100 pages. That book is 19 feet tall, and Alpöge’s proof is two and a half times longer.

In a recent development, despite the logic being verified as true through Lean code, Alpöge still has a major problem. So far, none of the mathematicians or researchers who have attempted to read it have been able to understand what it states.

According to recent reports, “I do not understand, and I suspect no human completely understands,” Jon Keating, professor of mathematical physics at the University of Oxford, stated in a Numberphile YouTube video. “When I look at that, I’m completely in awe and in wonderment.”.

For the problem to be fully solved, the proof has to be read, analyzed and simplified so that it can be translated into readable mathematics, which Alpöge states in his announcement that he’s in the process of doing. All of this has to be done so that Alpöge can publish it in a peer-reviewed journal in such a way that his peers can actually read it. It is only after the mathematics community scrutinizes and accepts Alpöge’s proof that it is considered fully solved.

Aside from being nigh unreadable to humans, Alpöge has otherwise avoided the kinds of drama that other AI-assisted discoveries have faced in 2026.

Industry observers note that openAI had to backtrack on its proof of the Navier-Stokes problem, which is another Millennium Problem, after the company couldn’t rule out that the AI models it used had access to data from other researchers. Somewhat ironically, one of those mathematicians whose work OpenAI may have  — knowingly or unknowingly — borrowed from was Levent Alpöge, as he and others were pretty close to solving the problem on their own.

Sources indicate that similarly, Claude was credited with finding a fresh novel enzyme that humans had never seen before. The problem is that computational biologist Mario Rodríguez Mestre had seen this enzyme before and was using Claude to study it further, so it’s uncertain if Claude actually found it independently or used data from Mestre’s research to find it.

In a recent development, the heavy assistance from AI has been met with mostly positive reactions, with most researchers agreeing that the AI usage is justified provided that the proof is proven to be true through peer review. Since no one was particularly close to solving the Riemann Hypothesis, there haven’t been any accusations of Alpöge or Claude stealing work like those prior examples. By and large, most mathematicians are excited about the discovery.

“Even before this, we have seen the power of AI, and this highlights that AI trained on hundreds of years of human mathematics can perform amazing tasks,” said Penn State’s Milewski. “I would add that AI didn’t come up with the Riemann Hypothesis, nor did most of the work to prove it, and AI probably doesn’t ‘know’ why it was invented or why it’s crucial.”.

According to recent reports, CNET spoke with a few professors about this, and they all echoed Milewski’s sentiment, stating that AI was trained with centuries of human mathematical achievement, so a win for AI is a win for humans too. Jeffrey Lagarias, a professor of mathematics at the University of Michigan, told CNET that “I don’t think this particular proof would have been found without AI.”.

Prasad Tetali, head of the department of mathematical sciences at Carnegie Mellon University, noted: “It is easy to overestimate the role of AI, and underappreciate decades of human mathematician work that went into it. The AI here is really standing tall and wide on the shoulders of generations of human giants.”.

On the AI side of things, influencers are attempting to use the news to hype up the capabilities of AI. Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang noted in a post on X that solving the Riemann Hypothesis was a sign that AI superintelligence was close at hand and that humanity should be terrified of the “alien mind that we don’t understand.”.

AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky likened the whole thing to a firm making enriched uranium that’ll one day result in the end of the human species.

It has been revealed that these warnings are hard to take seriously when one considers that Anthropic tried to make Claude solve the Riemann Hypothesis by itself back in August. Claude came up with some cool ideas but ultimately failed to solve the problem alone. For the time being, AI still needs a great deal of human guidance to make these massive discoveries, so the doom-and-gloom proselytizing comes off as a little premature.

According to recent reports, to make things even more interesting, a competing Riemann Hypothesis proof was submitted by Alessandro Masullo just a few hours after Alpöge released his. This competing proof is 940 pages long, which is significantly shorter than Alpöge’s proof, and it was an all-human effort with no AI assistance. The proof is months in the making, with Masullo working with mathematician Brian Conrad to bring it up to spec before it hits peer review. When Alpöge posted his proof, Masullo and others thought it wise to submit theirs as well.

This started a “dueling proofs” storyline over the weekend, but it was short-lived. Shortly after Masullo’s proof was posted, multiple people found the types of flaws and omissions that often disprove Riemann Hypothesis proofs. Those issues are in the process of being corrected, and the proof is officially in mid-revision status.

Masullo kept the original proof posted (PDF) in its unedited form, but acknowledges that the proof was rushed to publication so that it could compete with Alpöge and Claude.

“The PDF below was posted on Nov. 20 on Ravi Vakil’s blog,” Masullo wrote on a Google site. “It was never meant to be shared publicly at this stage, and it has been posted in this draft form in response to current circumstances.”.

It’s entirely possible that future revisions of Masullo’s work may solve the problems in the early draft and create a fully human proof of the Riemann Hypothesis without AI, but that isn’t happening anytime soon.

This is a lot of information about finding the Riemann Hypothesis, so it’s probably a good idea to briefly explain what it even is. In the 1730s, famous mathematician Leonhard Euler came up with a zeta function as a way to solve the Basel Problem, another mathematical curiosity about the exact sum of the reciprocals of squares. Euler was successful in this endeavor, and the zeta function became a part of mathematics.

Bernhard Riemann picked up where Euler left off and expanded the zeta function to use complex numbers — real numbers mixed with imaginary numbers — using a process called analytic continuation. Riemann used this expanded function to express how many prime numbers there were under a specific number and how tightly those prime numbers were packed together.

This is easy enough to do in your head with small numbers, like figuring out there are four prime numbers under 10, but when the biggest prime number is 41,024,320 digits long, having a function to do it for you is a lot more helpful.

The mechanics of Riemann’s expanded zeta function are quite complicated, and the math-focused YouTube channel Numberphile has an excellent explainer from a professional mathematician (with pictures) if you want to learn more.

Sources indicate that the hypothesis concerns the solutions the function yields. Riemann’s version of the zeta function showed that if you plugged in an even negative number, like -2, -4 or -672, the function would always spit out a zero. These are referred to as trivial zeroes, and Riemann proved that this was always true in his original paper.

Sources indicate that the Riemann Hypothesis is the conjecture that all the other numbers that would also make a zero — referred to as non-trivial zeroes — follow a very specific formula, which is “½ + it”, where “i” is an imaginary number and “t” is any real number, positive or negative. In short, Riemann believed that there was no other way to generate a zero with his zeta function other than even negative numbers (trivial zeroes) and numbers that followed the “½+it” formula (non-trivial zeroes). Riemann provided some examples of the hypothesis being right but never wrote a full proof of it.

Recent findings suggest that it’s worth noting that not every number that follows the “½+it” formula produces a zero, but that all the numbers that produce a zero will use that formula. It’s kind of the same as saying that all squares are rectangles but not all rectangles are squares.

Sources indicate that in the 167 years since the hypothesis was first published, mathematicians have found 12 trillion non-trivial zeroes, and every single one of them fits the above rules. Trillions of other numbers that don’t follow those rules have been tested to find a counterexample, since even one counterexample disproves the hypothesis immediately. Those efforts have produced no counterexamples at all.

Recent findings suggest that this isn’t conclusive proof, but it’s such an overwhelming amount of evidence that mathematicians began assuming that the hypothesis was true, even if no one could prove it. Alpöge’s AI-assisted proof is the first to show in any context that the hypothesis is always true, which, according to Tetali, has implications in prime number understanding, number theory and other branches of mathematics.

“The big job on the math side is to find a human-understandable proof,” Lagarias said. “I would say this is certainly going to happen; there will be such understanding. Already there are several AI digests of the proof breaking it into its component pieces. I have seen one [that’s] 11 pages, 164 pages, 273 pages. There are great ideas to extract from them.”.

Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, plan a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

It has been revealed that starting today, Google revealed, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

Once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

“You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response remarked, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

When I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

Since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to New York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

Also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

In a recent development, while Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.
