📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

According to recent reports, it’s a massive list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) plan to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL owners expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

It has been revealed that brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, states many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

“They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison says. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”.

Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

In a recent development, while Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how key it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison says BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

“With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he claims.

It has been revealed that not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

There are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

Long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

Pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

Sources indicate that harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL company doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

It has been revealed that because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

According to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL users had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison states.

According to recent reports, “If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he claims. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”.

Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

Still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison says, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

It has been revealed that “Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he claims. “There's a major difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A database containing about 2 billion login records for sites across the internet was accessible online without a password, security researcher Jeremiah Fowler noted in a report published Tuesday by ExpressVPN.
  • Recent findings suggest that the 2 billion figure is an estimate and not representative of the number of people affected, since some accounts may appear more than once and one person can have dozens of logins saved on a single device.
  • According to recent reports, fowler’s estimate of about 2 billion login records applies to the database he found.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A database containing about 2 billion login records for sites across the internet was accessible online without a password, security researcher Jeremiah Fowler noted in a report published Tuesday by ExpressVPN. The collection included usernames and passwords tied to email, social media, shopping and financial services. Among the files was an ad offering access to email accounts sorted by geography.

Recent findings suggest that the 2 billion figure is an estimate and not representative of the number of people affected, since some accounts may appear more than once and one person can have dozens of logins saved on a single device. Fowler reported the database to its hosting provider, which restricted public access several days later. It’s unclear how long the files had been exposed or who else may have accessed them.

According to recent reports, fowler’s estimate of about 2 billion login records applies to the database he found. Wired put the total at more than 3.5 billion by including a separate database that security firm UpGuard disclosed last week. That database held about 1.64 billion records, including Chinese national ID numbers, phone numbers and school enrollment records.

It has been revealed that some of the files Fowler reviewed appeared to be from infostealers — malicious software that collects saved passwords and other data from infected devices. Once that information is collected, brokers can buy it in bulk, sort it by country or account type and resell it in smaller batches. A buyer interested in email accounts in a particular country can pay for that slice of the data. The people selling it can make money from the same records more than once.

Fowler saw signs that the files came from multiple sources, but couldn’t determine who assembled the collection or whether it was used for sales, research or another purpose.

In a recent development, I saw a version of that business in my reporting on the dark web for CNET. On Genesis Market, buyers could shop for stolen accounts by location and category, including banking, email and social media. By the time authorities disrupted the marketplace in 2023, it had offered access to data from more than 1.5 million compromised computers, according to the Justice Department.

You can look up your email address in Have I Been Pwned to see whether it appears in a known data exposure. A clean result only tells you what’s in the service’s index.

If you see an unfamiliar login or suspect your device is infected, use a different, trusted device to change the affected password and sign out of other sessions. Start with your email if several accounts may be affected, since that’s where password reset links often go. Replace reused passwords with unique ones, use a password manager to keep track of them and turn on two-factor authentication where it’s available.

Recent findings suggest that identity theft protection services monitor for signs that your personal information has been exposed or misused. In a leak like this one, an alert about an exposed password can tell you which account to secure, especially if you’ve reused that password elsewhere. Aura is one of the services we tested for CNET’s guide to the best identity theft protection services.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The flood is too much for Tidal. The music streaming app announced on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated. The platform stated it’s making the move after being increasingly inundated with non-human music. As of Dec. 9, Tidal will no longer accept or host fully AI-generated tracks.

The app also noted distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.

According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov. 6 alone. Tidal said the affected tracks were labeled as AI and removed from the royalty pool, which is the pot of subscription and ad revenue paid out to rights holders.

In a recent development, before Tuesday’s action, Tidal had tried to lessen AI’s influence by identifying, labeling and demonetizing AI tracks, as outlined in its AI policy. But amid the growing influx of AI music, representatives for the app remarked it was time for “a more drastic change.”.

Tidal remarked there are 27 million tracks in its catalog that are 100% AI, but 96% of them have not been streamed at all in the past three months. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of Tidal’s entire listings.

The tech giant has removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for artist-name impersonation.

Recent findings suggest that some AI help is permitted. Musical tracks where the maker used AI assistance but did not rely on it to generate the entire track will be allowed on the platform. Tidal uses ⁠Ircam Amplify to detect AI.

Tidal didn’t specify how much AI help would be allowed.

A representative for Tidal didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Read more: I Only Listened to AI Music for a Week. It Was Terrible, but Not for the Reason You Think.

It has been revealed that “Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more,” the tech giant remarked in its announcement. “Everything in this patch comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for or copied by someone pretending to be you.”.

Generating music with AI is increasingly easy with online tools. The AI song-generation platform Suno can create songs using only text prompts. With Google’s Lyria, you can use photos or text prompts to generate tracks up to 3 minutes long.

Recent findings suggest that AI music also is not just about creating hit songs. Some industries need affordable music for short-form videos, games, apps and retail spaces, and they are increasingly turning to AI to supply it.

But streaming apps and other companies are fighting back against AI slop, which refers to often poor-quality AI-generated social media posts, articles, music, videos and images inundating the internet in an attempt to generate click-and-stream revenue.

Sources indicate that youTube recently rolled out a newly introduced labeling system to indicate which music is AI-generated. Deezer provides a free tool listeners can use to see which tracks are AI-generated. Spotify is labeling which musicians are AI and which are human. Apple is flagging AI-generated music so listeners can spot it.

Retiring in 2027? Here's How Much Cash You Need to Set Aside

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You'll often hear that it's important to continue investing during retirement.
  • You want your money to keep pace with inflation.
  • At the same time, it's key to have some cash on hand in case the market doesn't perform well.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Maurie Backman – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:22PM EST.

You'll often hear that it's important to continue investing during retirement. And the reason is simple.

You want your money to keep pace with inflation. If you pull your entire IRA or 401(k) out of the stock market and put it into cash, you might lose out on buying power through the years.

At the same time, it's key to have some cash on hand in case the market doesn't perform well. And if you're retiring in 2027, now's the time to secure that cash reserve before you start living off your portfolio.

Industry observers note that the reason you need a pile of cash in retirement is simple. You never know what the stock market is going to do on any given day.

According to recent reports, if you're at a point in life when you're using your portfolio for income, you may not have the luxury to wait months or years for a recovery. Your bills need to get paid now.

Sources indicate that if you set aside a cash reserve, you'll be able to leave your investments alone during a stock market downturn. That means instead of locking in permanent losses, you'll give your portfolio a chance to recover. If you don't keep some cash on hand and your bills can't wait, you could end up selling assets at a loss, increasing the risk of depleting your savings.

While it's crucial to have some cash available in retirement, you don't want to go overboard. Keeping too much cash on hand could mean losing out on stronger returns.

As a general rule of thumb, you may want to aim for one to three years' worth of living expenses in cash. That gives you time to ride out a prolonged market downturn. The exact amount you land on should hinge on how much peace of mind you want and what your spending and non-portfolio income sources look like.

If you're the type to lose sleep over a stock market crash, a three-year cushion may be best. On the other hand, if your budget is flexible, you have generous Social Security benefits coming your way, and you're open to working to supplement your income when needed, a one-year cash cushion may be enough.

Either way, if your retirement date is getting closer, start strategically moving assets into cash now. Decide on the amount you need, and shop around for a high-yield savings account so you can earn a decent return on your money.

You may also want to look at a CD ladder if you'll be setting aside a larger amount of cash, like two to three years' worth. If you set up those CDs to mature at regular intervals, you can retain access to your cash while potentially earning a higher return than a regular savings account.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

Recent findings suggest that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

In a recent development, “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

In a recent development, this afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under upcoming management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

Tech Report: Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Neocloud firm CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

Recent findings suggest that recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

Chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

"CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," stated Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

Industry observers note that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and upcoming markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security firm, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

According to recent reports, in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Sources indicate that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

According to recent reports, overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the firm if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he remarked. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

"Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," remarked Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
  • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
  • An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

Industry observers note that an interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any issues are documented.

A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

According to recent reports, service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

In a recent development, inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

Detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

Industry observers note that the good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

Recent findings suggest that however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

It has been revealed that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

Industry observers note that reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that reddit people are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several customers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

Another concern is the accumulation of investors holding positions at substantially higher prices. As cryptocurrencies attempt to recover, investors looking to exit at smaller losses could introduce additional selling pressure. For Bitcoin, the $70,000 to $75,000 range may prove particularly challenging, while Ethereum and Solana face similar obstacles after breaking through important price levels during the recent downturn.

Industry observers note that looking ahead, the broader macroeconomic environment remains an important risk. #108838. Breaking: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1027 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1027 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

According to recent reports, the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he remarked.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That stated, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

"There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

It has been revealed that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she stated.

The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

Industry observers note that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he said. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

"It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she remarked.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

In a recent development, but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

"We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin noted. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

Industry observers note that it's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

"That's when spreads really widen out," he noted. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that A turnaround at a major operating unit, estimates-beating numbers, and a raise in profitability guidance powered Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS +14.59%) stock to a double-digit gain on Tuesday.
  • Here's a look at how Dick's did overall and whether investors can expect further gains from the veteran athletic-gear purveyor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Eric Volkman – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:31PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Dick's Sporting Goods ›.

It has been revealed that A turnaround at a major operating unit, estimates-beating numbers, and a raise in profitability guidance powered Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS +14.59%) stock to a double-digit gain on Tuesday. The specialty retailer's third quarter not only featured better-than-expected financials but also growth from the struggling brand it acquired last year.

Here's a look at how Dick's did overall and whether investors can expect further gains from the veteran athletic-gear purveyor.

Industry observers note that dick's net sales in the quarter were $5.13 billion, 23% higher year over year. The caveat to this is the mentioned brand, Foot Locker, which the company acquired in 2025. That acquisition closed in early September of that year; as a result, only 8 weeks of Foot Locker's results were consolidated into Dick's third-quarter 2025 accounting -- hence the major difference between last third quarter's sales and this one.

Stripping Foot Locker out of the equation, the manufacturer's comparable sales rose by 2.6% in the quarter. Dick's mentioned this was largely due to a rise in average ticket (i.e., average customer spending per transaction), offset by a slight decline in the number of transactions. On a pro forma basis, Foot Locker posted a 0.5% improvement. On a consolidated, pro forma basis for the company as a whole, comparable sales were 1.8% higher.

Turning to profitability, non-GAAP (adjusted) net income came in at $167.5 million, or $1.94 per share. That was down from $180.6 million in the year-ago quarter.

It has been revealed that despite the bottom-line slide, Dick's easily beat the consensus analyst estimates. Prognosticators tracking the firm were modeling net sales of $5.08 billion, and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of merely $1.42.

According to recent reports, while those key fundamentals headed in an encouraging direction, it was Foot Locker's performance that really won the race for Dick's. That 0.5% increase in the brand's "comps" is quite an achievement -- it's the first time since the acquisition that it's been in the black.

Previously, many investors had considered it to be a laggard. The unit didn't seem like a potential winner at all, with its 3.6% decrease in pro forma comps only one quarter ago.

It still has some distance to run. In the conference call discussing the third-quarter results, management stated that Foot Locker performed particularly well in its core U.S. operating unit, which delivered comps of 4.1%. But the overall number was dragged down by sluggish performance in the Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) super-region. The brand was also burdened by high inventory levels, which required discounting to reduce.

Industry observers note that another negative for Foot Locker is Nike's (NKE +5.89%) reset of its storied Jordan sneaker brand, which is aging and suffers from oversupply. Like any major brand overhaul, this will take some time -- Nike flagged fiscal 2029 for Jordan to return to growth. Nike footwear is a major draw within Foot Locker's product selection.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

Given that, Dick's maintained its guidance for full-year Foot Locker sales and comps. Specifically, it's expecting the unit to contribute $7.4 billion to $7.5 billion to the top line, with comparable sales expected to be flat to 2% down. Its operating loss should range from $40 million to $80 million.

But the core Dick's business should compensate for this. Management raised the low end of the unit's net sales forecast from $14.5 billion to $14.6 billion, maintaining the high end of $14.7 billion. Ditto for comps, now expected to be 3.3% to 4% (previously 2.5% at the bottom end).

All in all, the tech giant is expecting a prosperous year. With the boosts to the Dick's unit estimates, the company's overall guidance is higher. The new floor for overall net sales is $22 billion (formerly $21.9 billion), with the maximum holding steady at $22.2 billion. Better, adjusted EPS is now anticipated to land at $11.45 to $12.30, up notably from the preceding forecast of $11 to $12.

So, can we consider Dick's stock a buy candidate? I think much will depend on Foot Locker, which, given its size, has a significant impact on its parent's results. Despite investor excitement over the brand’s positive third-quarter comps figure, it still needs to improve sufficiently to become a regular, meaningful contributor to overall company growth. It has to work through its inventory concerns and develop strategies to grow during the "Jordan gap.".

Sources indicate that that said, Dick's stock offers a high-yield dividend (presently paying 3.3%) that appears quite sustainable, and its core business is performing well. I also like the rather modest forward P/E of under 13. To me, these factors make the shares attractive, but more for those with a relatively long-term investment horizon.

According to recent reports, premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

According to recent reports, “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Sources indicate that dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Breaking: What Are Repositioning Cruises?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
  • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
  • Industry observers note that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

Industry observers note that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

According to recent reports, one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

According to recent reports, another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

Sources indicate that just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a upcoming region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

According to recent reports, repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit crucial sites when off the ship.

Sources indicate that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

According to recent reports, for ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy highlights, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Recent findings suggest that many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

Industry observers note that if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

Sources indicate that here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

It has been revealed that this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between New York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

Departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and New England before reaching the Major Apple.

Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching New York.

I am optimistic about Ethereum in the long term -- as the biggest smart-contract crypto, it is well-positioned to benefit from any growth in the stablecoin and real-world asset tokenization markets. However, I am less optimistic about Bitmine because the treasury model carries too many risks, including share dilution, liquidation, and management changes. Ethereum ETFs allow investors to access Ethereum through their brokerage accounts and custody solutions, without the risks associated with treasury companies.

#108829. ​Building A Data Foundation That Makes Enterprise AI Work

AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

​Building A Data Foundation That Makes Enterprise AI Work

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (761 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Niraj Nagrani is Chief Data and AI Officer at Altimetrik.
  • According to recent reports, after more than 30 years as an enterprise leader, I’ve been through many transformation journeys, from building hyperscale systems and training data for machine learning to migrating from legacy architectures to modern data platforms.
  • The problem is not with foundation models, which have improved exponentially over the past few years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Niraj Nagrani is Chief Data and AI Officer at Altimetrik.

According to recent reports, after more than 30 years as an enterprise leader, I’ve been through many transformation journeys, from building hyperscale systems and training data for machine learning to migrating from legacy architectures to modern data platforms. Today, I see many organizations struggle to move from a successful AI pilot to a reliable production system​.

The problem is not with foundation models, which have improved exponentially over the past few years. In my experience, the problem almost always comes back to the underlying data architecture.

Many organizations are still working with data that isn’t ready for AI. Data quality and lineage may be governed inconsistently or not governed at all. And governance is often bolted on at the end rather than built in from the start.

I’ve worked with companies running over 100 siloed systems. When information is scattered that widely, it can be almost impossible to establish a consistent view of the business. Unstructured data like contracts, emails and support tickets can disappear into blind spots because they don’t fit neatly into traditional data structures. Another problem is the lack of a shared definition of business entities like revenue, customers or other vital measures across systems. ​.

Sources indicate that earlier machine learning learned patterns from a curated, labeled dataset to do one narrow task. Agents reason and act in real time across systems. At the moment of action, an agent has to know what a “customer” means, which policy applies, whether the data is current and what it is allowed to see. Without that context, you get a confident wrong action. Earlier machine learning needed clean training data; agents need living context.

It has been revealed that the key first step of data modernization is what I call “business rule archaeology.” Over time, organizations accumulate business logic in stored procedures, SQL queries and their dependencies. Some of that logic is documented, but a lot of it isn’t, which makes it difficult to understand how the existing business processes actually work. Companies often underestimate the effort required to untangle these dependencies.​.

Industry observers note that before planning for​ modernization, understand how the business uses its data and how its processes operate. From there, organizations can build an incremental migration blueprint rather than trying to move everything at once.​.

According to recent reports, ​I think about modernization as four steps, and each one becomes a layer of the platform you end up with. First, unify the isolated systems in an open lakehouse built on object storage and open table formats such as Iceberg or Delta, holding one governed copy of structured and unstructured data. Feed it through streaming and change data capture, because agents need current information, not last night’s batch.

Second, define shared business definitions in a semantic layer, so “revenue” or “customer” means the same thing in every system. Third, capture how those entities relate in an ontology and knowledge graph. This is what gives an agent the context for its decisions. Fourth, put governed retrieval across structured and unstructured data, with governance as code providing access management, lineage and a replayable audit trail. Agents also need their own identities with least-privilege access, and cost controls belong in the design from the start, because the cost of running models decides what is affordable at scale.​.

Data trust is crucial, but it’s especially challenging when different teams have different standards for what good data looks like. Trust is an interface problem you engineer: one definition, enforced in the pipeline.

One useful mechanism is a data contract, a machine-readable agreement covering schema, quality requirements and service-level expectations between producer and consumer. It functions like a stable API, making the relationship between those parties more predictable.

In a recent development, ​Another is shift-left governance. Instead of checking lineage, quality and policy at the review end of a process, organizations should embed those requirements as code where data is produced. Privacy, risk and compliance rules belong in that code too, with identity and access management deciding which people and agents can see each dataset.​.

In a recent development, many current operating systems and data warehouses were built to answer yesterday’s question for a human. An agent-ready platform has to serve decisions to a machine in real time, with context, semantics and governance built into its design. That is what matters most as we design the next generation of data platform architecture.​.

Sources indicate that another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

Sources indicate that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

According to recent reports, the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

My point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

In a recent development, here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

It has been revealed that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

It has been revealed that mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

Sources indicate that strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI indicated wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

According to recent reports, predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

In a recent development, markets are currently anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:41PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

Sources indicate that with Bitcoin (BTC -3.49%) collapsing below $60,000 on Nov. 20 to hit $55,081 the next day as the Nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) drama continued, it's worth pondering whether this is a good opportunity to buy the dip, or if it's a trap for those who refuse to recognize that the market is turning against it.

On Nov. 23, Jensen Huang's return as CEO lifted Nvidia's shares by 27%, but Bitcoin by only 0.6%, and the coin fell back beneath the $60,000 level within 24 hours anyway. In other words, it lost more during volatility that was mostly unrelated to it than it was able to regain once its trigger reversed.

According to recent reports, this isn't the first time that dynamic has reared its head, and it tends to make the idea of buying future dips a bit less attractive. Let's dive in and analyze the situation.

The lopsided response that disfavors Bitcoin is somewhat attributable to who was selling it and the duration of their holding.

Most of November's sellers had held their coins for under six months. Their losses, measured against past-year profits, reached levels seen only near the 2018, 2020, 2022, and early 2023 lows. Such capitulation, which is to say panicked bulk selling at a loss, often sends prices well below what the news actually justifies -- and in this case, Nvidia's problems are mostly distinct from Bitcoin's, but the justified fears of a potential incoming rate hike by the Federal Reserve are not.

Nonetheless, dip buyers picked up about 66,000 BTC when it was priced between $62,000 and $66,000, only to see that price floor break within a week. Their losses may well be erased if they hold for the long term, but for now, they're underwater, which may make it stressful or unappealing for some investors to buy the slightly deeper dip this time around.

Now let's hear the other side of the argument. The Nov. 21 low comes four years to the day after the coin's 2022 bear market bottom. If the four-year cyclical rhythm of Bitcoin continues, that timing favors buyers.

According to recent reports, the next halving, which halves new coin output, is due in April 2028. Bitcoin has historically bottomed out 12 to 18 months before a halving. That puts the window for the bottom between about October 2026 and April 2027, so those who buy the dip now could be well-positioned for that bull run, if it occurs.

Recent findings suggest that the market is obviously disfavoring the coin compared to other investments, and it has been doing so for a while. It only grew by 6% over the last five years. Its core investment thesis is still valid, but there could still be downside from here.

Thus, I'm interested in buying some Bitcoin here, but only with a small amount of capital, and only because I know I'm willing to hold it for many years to come.

Compass Minerals provides customers with a variety of notable minerals, such as salt products used to keep roads safe in winter weather, and its plant nutrition products help improve crop quality and yield while supporting sustainable agriculture.

Sources indicate that after encountering operational challenges several years ago -- including its decision to cancel its lithium project in Utah -- Compass Minerals is showing signs of success in its efforts to get back on track. Plus, the tech giant ended fiscal 2026 in better financial health, reducing its adjusted net debt-to-trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA ratio to 3.2 as of Sept. 30, 2026, down from 3.9 at the same time last year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
  • According to recent reports, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
  • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

According to recent reports, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

There are four main types of grants:.

Federal grants come from the federal government.

State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

In a recent development, to receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

Recent findings suggest that federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

It has been revealed that some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

Sources indicate that after you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

Sources indicate that most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal proposal.

In a recent development, in some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

According to recent reports, grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

Some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

Sources indicate that after your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment looks, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

According to recent reports, to maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

Your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

It has been revealed that yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

You withdrew from your program.

You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

It depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

Recent findings suggest that if you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

Sources indicate that grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge. Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking stable income can consider enhancing their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

Industry observers note that however, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Tracking the ratings of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as their recommendations are backed by in-depth research.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Sources indicate that chord Energy is an independent exploration and production firm with long-lived assets primarily in the Williston Basin. With a quarterly base dividend of $1.30 per share, CHRD offers a dividend yield of 3.67%.

In a research note on third-quarter expectations, RBC Capital analyst Scott Hanold reiterated a buy rating on CHRD stock with a price target of $175. "We model production near the top of guidance and continue to see strong performance from new wells and base production," remarked Hanold.

Specifically, the five-star analyst expects Q3 2026 production at 283 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or Mboe/d, in line with the Street's consensus and near the high end of the 278 to 284 Mboe/d guidance. Hanold remarked his Q3 2026 earnings per share estimate increased to $5.29 due to lower non-cash depreciation, depletion and amortization.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, cash flow per share estimate moved lower to $13.59 to reflect Hanold's revision based on the current backdrop and commodity mark-to-market. He expects Chord Energy to report capital spending of $375 million for Q3 2026, slightly above the Street's estimate of $369 million.

In a recent development, overall, Hanold remains bullish on CHRD, given its best-in-class balance sheet. He expects a free cash flow payout of 80% in the third quarter, with the possibility of an upside. Hanold expects investors to focus on management commentary on 2027 capital plans, Williston M&A opportunities, and long-term performance of 4-mile wells.

Industry observers note that hanold ranks No. 310 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Chord Energy KPIs on TipRanks.

At a quarterly dividend of $0.5250 per share, Williams offers a yield of 2.89%.

It has been revealed that in her latest research note, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $87. Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, the analyst mentioned that she expects WMB to announce strong quarterly performance.

Scotto raised her estimates to reflect insights from the quarterly catch-up call, the completion of the Momentum Midstream acquisition, and mark-to-market quarter-to-date commodity prices. She expects WMB to report Q3 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2,036 million, which is modestly above the Street's consensus estimate.

The analyst expects the organization's Q3 cash flow per share to exceed the Street's consensus by 13%, driven by better-than-expected production.

Byrne expects crude oil production, excluding the UAE, to reach 551 Mboe/d, which is at the high end of guidance (546-551 Mboe/d) and above the Street's projection of 548 Mboe/d, driven by continued growth in the Utica.

Furthermore, Byrne expects cash operating expenses to come in at $10.27 per barrel of oil equivalent, below the midpoint of guidance of $10.05 to $11.35, helped by lower lease operating expenses. Overall, the analyst expects EOG to deliver free cash flow of $2.65 billion, supporting another quarter of buybacks near the minimum 70% shareholder return threshold and implying about $1.5 billion in share repurchases.

"As a first indication of the '27 strategy, we expect EOG will message another year of mid-single-digit (~3.5%) growth on a flat capital budget (~$6.55bn), which is above the Street modeling 1% oil growth at $6.6bn," mentioned Byrne.
