#108809. 19 Signs Your Tech giant’s Technology Is Creating More Work

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1381 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

19 Signs Your Tech giant’s Technology Is Creating More Work

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1381 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that technology should simplify workflows and improve productivity.
  • These workarounds can reveal deeper problems with technology adoption, system design and organizational processes.
  • According to recent reports, the biggest tell for me is hearing, “Here’s how we actually do it.” If that follows with some description that combines spreadsheets, duplicate data entry, manual handoffs or clever ways around the system, that’s a pretty clear sign the technology is creating work rather than removing it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that technology should simplify workflows and improve productivity. However, when systems are difficult to navigate, unreliable or disconnected, employees may develop alternative solutions just to get their jobs done.

These workarounds can reveal deeper problems with technology adoption, system design and organizational processes. Below, Forbes Technology Council members share warning signs that employees are spending too much time working around their tech giant’s technology rather than benefiting from it, along with insights on addressing the underlying concerns.

According to recent reports, the biggest tell for me is hearing, “Here’s how we actually do it.” If that follows with some description that combines spreadsheets, duplicate data entry, manual handoffs or clever ways around the system, that’s a pretty clear sign the technology is creating work rather than removing it. - Abhijit Singh, Jefferson.

According to recent reports, if employees constantly ask coworkers for help with the same system tasks or there’s an unofficial cheat sheet, chat thread or go-to “expert” everyone relies on to navigate a tool, the technology is not intuitive enough to be used on its own. Low adoption of mandatory tools or latest hires taking too long to be productive with a tool are indicators that people are spending too much time figuring out the technology instead of using it. - Austin Berglas, Nardello & Co.

Industry observers note that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Working around a system can increase your cognitive load—the mental effort placed on your working memory. A recent survey found that since AI was introduced, enterprise workers spend longer searching for information, parse through more alerts, and juggle more tabs and applications. Symptoms like these can indicate employees are working harder to manage the technology than realizing its benefits. - Mazy Dar, HERE Enterprise (here.io).

Jumping across multiple tools and screens to complete one workflow is a clear sign that people are just becoming workers for the tools rather than using those tools to deliver their work better and faster. This is more relevant in the AI era. - Raja Shanmugam, TATA Consultancy Services.

When employees rely on personal texts, phone calls or spreadsheets to compensate for enterprise systems, there’s a workflow problem. These workarounds often emerge because existing tools are too slow, fragmented or unreliable. Leaders should investigate where employees bypass technology and address the underlying friction before it creates operational risks. - Judit Sharon, OnPage Corporation.

Industry observers note that watch for employees delaying decisions because they don’t trust how current the information is. If a sales or marketing team has to wait for an overnight revision before responding to a customer or adjusting a campaign, the technology is setting the pace instead of supporting the work. Teams should be able to act on what is happening now, not yesterday’s picture. - Vibhor Kapoor, AdRoll.

One sign is that unofficial spreadsheets become essential to completing everyday work. In capital markets, employees may repeatedly export trade data, reconcile it manually, and re-enter the results across systems. When these workarounds become routine, the technology is shifting effort onto employees rather than removing it. Those spreadsheets reveal where workflows need fixing. - Lakshmanan Alagappan, Genpact UK.

Shadow documentation is a sign that the official documentation is lacking or so generic that it is hard to adapt to use cases that are fairly common. The more guides that are built to explain how to use a piece of software, the more it should be evaluated for improvement. Simplify the interface with role-based views, and rename custom fields and data so they’re clearer. Just don’t forget to clean up the shadow documentation too. - Luke Wallace, Bottle Rocket.

Industry observers note that one sign is that the know-how lives in people, not the system. When a tool doesn’t do exactly what’s needed, rather than asking for changes to the tool, work becomes manual, and one person ends up as the only one who knows how it really runs. Sometimes that’s accidental and sometimes it’s job security; either way, it’s a bottleneck. - Anila Siraj, OpsBridge Advisory.

It has been revealed that one sign is employees building integrations the vendor never intended. Not plugins. Not configurations. Custom code written at midnight by someone who needed two systems to talk to each other and could not wait six months for a roadmap update. That unauthorized integration is not ingenuity. It is your architecture silently fracturing one undocumented API call at a time. When engineers route around the system, the system has already failed. - Mukul Arora.

Sources indicate that people clicking straight through warnings is a sign. Track override rates and fix the friction behind them. If employees routinely hit “proceed anyway” on a blocked link or a security prompt, the tool is getting in the way of real work, and they have stopped reading it. That is a workaround too, albeit a quiet one, and it trains them to ignore warnings—maybe even those that matter. - Flavius Plesu, OutThink.

One clear sign is when employees spend more time figuring out how to make a tool work than doing their actual jobs. If everyone knows which buttons to avoid, which errors to ignore and when to restart the system, your technology isn’t saving time. It’s wasting it. - Margarita Simonova, ILoveMyQA.

Check the expense reports, not the help desk tickets. When employees start reimbursing themselves for $30 SaaS subscriptions, they’ve already given up on the official tools and bought their way around them. Finance sees it first. IT sees it months later. The line items are small enough to approve without question, which is exactly why they keep adding up. - Nidhi Jain, CloudEagle.ai.

Recent findings suggest that map the value stream from user intent to task outcome. If employees are required to navigate more than three non-value-added steps to complete a task, I’d question the process before adding more steps. Workarounds add effort yet little to no customer value. Even worse is when teams automate workarounds when they should be eliminating the reason it exists in the first place. - April Ho-Nishimura, Infineon Technologies AG.

It has been revealed that when I ask a client team how their leadership report is produced, a common answer is that someone builds a spreadsheet by hand before every meeting. That tells me the official systems are being worked around. The hours are the visible cost. The bigger one is that leaders start questioning the numbers in the room instead of making decisions. - Dimitar Dimitrov, Accedia.

Count the decisions the technology changed last week. Many companies hand managers a data platform and announce that every number is in there, ready for any table they want. Almost nobody opens it because it asks them to become analysts. They keep deciding using their gut and old reports. A tool that shows each manager their own score and the next move gets checked daily. If a system doesn’t trigger decisions, it is overhead. - Vivek Thomas, AISensum.

In a recent development, you must watch how often employees double-check a tool’s output before acting on it. If a manager has to pull the original records to verify every report, the system may be saving time on preparation while adding it back in review. So, ask what people still check by hand and why. That extra checking is part of the cost of the tool, too. - Elton Chan, Second Talent.

According to recent reports, take a construction site where the real system is WhatsApp. A delivery gets redirected to another site in a group chat; nobody updates the records, materials arrive at the wrong site, and machinery stands idle. When orders change in chats and handwritten logs, the ERP is just a reporting duty. Count how many changes never reach your system of record. - Andrew Babkin, Azati.

One sign is when employees lower the quality of their work because organization technology cannot support enough detail. Engineers may simplify technical assessments, while customer service teams may give incomplete responses because systems restrict what they can record or process. Leaders should check whether technology limitations influence the quality of business outcomes. Technology should support professional judgment, not force employees to compromise it. - Salice Thomas, Wipro Limited.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for upcoming Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

According to recent reports, among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their upcoming season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

Industry observers note that the scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the latest season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

Recent findings suggest that that goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

It has been revealed that thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Industry observers note that everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

In a recent development, everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

It has been revealed that the Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Recent findings suggest that joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The major Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Sources indicate that ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Recent findings suggest that half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

In a recent development, everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

According to recent reports, good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

It has been revealed that joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

According to recent reports, newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Newcastle get the game under way.

Sources indicate that bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

According to recent reports, we know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Recent findings suggest that significant Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX.

According to recent reports, A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula.

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade.

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg.

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry.

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl.

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

It has been revealed that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

In a recent development, “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about fresh signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle remarked he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

Sources indicate that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

Industry observers note that the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Industry observers note that furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

It has been revealed that wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

According to recent reports, wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

It has been revealed that heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

It has been revealed that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active consumers in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently debuted Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

According to recent reports, next is semiconductor firm Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

Sources indicate that the five-star analyst mentioned that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

Sources indicate that while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

In a recent development, svanberg mentioned that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. According to recent reports, first, though, let's take a look at the Nvidia story so far, including the recent turmoil. Nvidia has trailblazed in AI, with its early entry into the AI chip market and innovations that have kept it ahead of rivals. This has resulted in jaw-dropping earnings growth, and this deep involvement in AI has transformed Jensen Huang into an expert in the field. His knowledge and visibility about what's ahead have made him a valuable asset -- and one that investors weren't eager to replace.

It has been revealed that that's why when he resigned following allegations of two affairs, the stock slid, and investors questioned the ability of the manufacturer to continue with the same momentum. Huang's reinstatement reassured investors, as we can see through the stock's performance. It's key to keep in mind, however, that Nvidia isn't out of the woods yet. The company is investigating Huang's relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence says is a spy for China. And lawmakers have called for Huang to testify on the matter -- that should unfold early next month. Meanwhile, press reports say that regulators have opened a probe into Nvidia's accounting practices.

It has been revealed that all of this, as well as investors' growing caution regarding AI, may periodically weigh on the stock price. Recent findings suggest that so, now, let's consider how much Nvidia may be worth with Jensen Huang back in the leadership role. Analysts upgraded the stock following Huang's return, and most price targets landed considerably above $200, with one even at $270, according to CNBC. That said, price targets are generally for a 12-month period, so this doesn't mean Nvidia will reach these levels tomorrow. In fact, the stock might face volatility in the weeks and months to come, considering the investigations I mentioned above as well as the general concerns weighing on AI stocks.

As I mentioned above, a number of headwinds could impact stock performance and slow the firm's path to the price targets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Recent findings suggest that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the substantial positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the upcoming year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

Industry observers note that “I feel like the club is in a fresh era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

Industry observers note that PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:12PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Everspin Technologies ›.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Everspin (MRAM -7.37%) reported record quarterly revenue of $20.6 million driven by a 34% year-over-year surge in product sales. This growth signals expanding commercial adoption of Magnetoresistive Random-Access Memory, or MRAM, a specialized type of computer memory that retains data even when power is turned off. For long-term investors, the company's ability to defend gross margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining after direct manufacturing costs, while expanding into critical markets provides a clear test of its competitive position.

Three things management said stand out.

Rising input costs weighed on product profitability during the third quarter, prompting management to raise prices across its product lineup starting in the fourth quarter. Long-term profitability hinges on whether customers accept these price increases without reducing order volumes.

Demand for MRAM is accelerating in life-critical medical devices such as dialysis machines, infusion pumps, and defibrillators where memory failure cannot be tolerated. Expanding into mission-critical applications creates sticky, long-term customer relationships with high switching costs.

According to recent reports, management demonstrated the world's first Compute Express Link, or CXL, connected MRAM, an open industry standard that connects processors and memory at high speeds. By establishing standard interfaces for persistent memory in artificial intelligence workloads and leading industry standards groups, Everspin opens larger addressable markets.

Product momentum in low Earth orbit satellites and automated industrial factories continues to gain traction, and management indicates clear momentum in commercializing next-generation memory designs. Manufacturing partnerships, including process transfer efforts at a semiconductor fabrication facility in Gresham, Oregon, offer scalable long-term capacity. Management is watching the transition of recent engineering design wins into high-volume commercial production while maintaining pricing discipline.

Long-term value creation depends on expanding beyond niche industrial uses into broad computing architectures without sacrificing profitability. Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The tech giant has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. It has been revealed that in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the tech giant's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

In a recent development, specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

Sources indicate that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

    There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

    Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

    You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

    In a recent development, it was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

    Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

    Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

    Recent findings suggest that the one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward promptly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

    The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

    It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

    Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

    Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

    There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

    Sources indicate that you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

    It has been revealed that top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

    Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

    He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

    It has been revealed that leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

    In a recent development, it was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

    Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

    It has been revealed that the misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

The goal they have just scored is indicative of how they have started and it’s a positive for Joshua Zirkzee, who has spent much of his time at Old Trafford under a cloud, to have finished it with aplomb. Whether it will be enough to keep him at Old Trafford for the long run remains to be seen, particularly as interest from Italy persists, but what can’t be doubted is his attitude. He looks sharp.

    It has been revealed that good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

    It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

    This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in Fresh Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

    While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

    10 stocks we like better than Everest Group ›.

    Sources indicate that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Everest Group (EG +1.12%) announced that its reserve buffer reached over $850 million above actuarial central estimates. This balance sheet cushion protects future earnings from rising litigation costs in third-party liability coverage.

    Three key takeaways from management's comments stand out for long-term investors.

    Management reinforced casualty lines, which protect policyholders against third-party liability claims, while withholding favorable returns from short-tail property contracts that cover immediate physical damage. By increasing reserves above central actuarial estimates, the company aims to eliminate future earnings volatility from historical claims.

    It has been revealed that the company shrank reinsurance premiums in liability contracts by 18% as competitive pressures pushed market rates below target return thresholds. Management prefers protecting profit margins over chasing top-line volume when competitors underprice structural risks.

    Industry observers note that capital deployment prioritizes direct stock buybacks alongside regular quarterly dividend payments. Management repurchased $474 million of common stock during the quarter, bringing year-to-date total capital returns above $1.4 billion.

    Competitive intensity is rising across primary insurance lines, but pricing discipline and lead-market status shield long-term returns. Operating units are expanding international specialty lines while lowering probable maximum losses from catastrophic weather events.

    Portfolio optimization and proactive balance sheet management position the business to generate consistent compounding value across changing market cycles.

    • Recent findings suggest that ambarella makes low-power chips that run artificial intelligence directly on devices such as security cameras, car safety systems, drones and dashcams.
    • But what spooked investors were the projections: For the fourth quarter, which ends Jan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:27PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Ambarella ›.

    According to recent reports, ambarella (AMBA -19.96%) shares plummeted 38% to $27 in after-hours trading Tuesday after the chipmaker warned that a worldwide memory shortage is hurting demand for its products. Nasdaq halted trading in the stock at 4:01 p.m. ET ahead of the news.

    Recent findings suggest that ambarella makes low-power chips that run artificial intelligence directly on devices such as security cameras, car safety systems, drones and dashcams. Revenue for the third quarter, which ended Oct. 31, rose 6% to $115.2 million, while adjusted earnings rose to $0.28 per share from $0.27 a year earlier.

    But what spooked investors were the projections: For the fourth quarter, which ends Jan. 31, Ambarella expects revenue of $70 million to $75 million. That's a drop of 35% to 39% from the quarter it just reported.

    It has been revealed that "The unprecedented rise in memory prices and the scarcity of memory supply we previously highlighted has intensified and is causing many customers to reduce their outlooks," CEO Fermi Wang said in the release. He added that third-quarter revenue landed at the low end of the company's guidance range because consumer device sales came in below expectations.

    It has been revealed that ambarella doesn't make memory, but almost every device that uses its chips also needs memory chips. When memory becomes scarce and expensive, the camera and car electronics makers that buy from Ambarella build fewer products or delay them, and they order fewer Ambarella chips.

    Ambarella isn't the only company feeling it this week. Hewlett Packard Enterprise CEO Antonio Neri noted on Monday's earnings call that he expects memory supply to stay constrained until at least the second half of 2028. On Tuesday, HP Inc. said in its earnings release that it is "taking steps to address memory and storage cost pressures.".

    Industry observers note that ambarella guided for adjusted operating expenses of $57.5 million to $59.5 million in the fourth quarter, with an adjusted gross margin of 59% to 60.25%. At the midpoints, that works out to about $43 million in gross profit against roughly $58.5 million in expenses, resulting in an adjusted operating loss of about $15 million. Using the organization's third-quarter figures, which leave out stock-based compensation and acquisition costs the same way its guidance does, Ambarella earned an adjusted operating profit of about $11 million.

    According to recent reports, the company expects to keep its overall spending roughly level even as revenue drops, and it has the cash to do so. It ended the quarter with $282.8 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, up from $272.3 million three months earlier.

    Ambarella had been flagging the problem for months. Its March annual report listed memory shortages as a possibility. By its June quarterly report, it noted there "have been tightening supply conditions in the memory market." In September's quarterly report, it added that tighter memory supply "could have an impact on" customers' demand for its products.

    The earnings release 8-K that came out a day earlier didn't mention memory specifically at all. It forecast third-quarter revenue of $115 million to $124 million. Ambarella came in at $115.2 million, the bottom of that range.

    Wang tried to separate the shortage from the long-term story. Memory problems "do not have an impact on our very positive secular growth outlook for edge AI," he said, and he expects the tech giant's fiscal 2028, which begins in February, "to be a growth year.".

    According to recent reports, that's a claim worth assessing. Ambarella states many of its customers are lowering their outlooks while memory stays scarce and expensive, and if HPE's view holds, that may not ease until at least the second half of 2028. Wang also noted edge AI revenue hit a record in the third quarter, so the demand for AI on devices is real. The question is how long the memory squeeze keeps it from turning into sales.

    In a recent development, for investors in semiconductor stocks, Ambarella's warning is a reminder that the AI boom comes at a cost to companies outside the data center, with the same memory demand that's filling orders for AI servers draining supply from smaller device makers. Until Ambarella shows its revenue can recover, its stock is likely to trade on headlines about memory prices (as HPE and Dell did on Tuesday), and buyers looking for a turnaround in AI may want to wait for next quarter's guidance.

    #108745. Industry News: Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2481 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2481 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, it's not the point of the video, I know.
    • What you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of Upcoming York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass.
    • That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, it's not the point of the video, I know. The clip the Fresh York Knicks posted late Sunday night was intended to celebrate Josh Hart producing arguably his best performance in what's been a rocky start to the season — 10 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists and a steal, his 18th triple-double in a Knicks uniform, tied for the second-most in franchise history — in a 113-106 win over the rival Indiana Pacers at Madison Square Garden.

    What you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of Upcoming York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass. And at the very start of the clip, before the camera pans over to Hart, there's only one Knicks player in sight: Karl-Anthony Towns.

    That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.

    The early-season MVP conversation pretty much starts and ends with Victor Wembanyama and Luka Dončić, the scoreboard-breaking titans leading the top two squads in the Western Conference. Expand the parameters out a little bit, though, and Towns — whose contract Knicks owner James L. Dolan declined to extend before the start of the season, and man, does it sure seem like the price is going up with every passing game — is forcing his way into the tier below them.

    In a recent development, the Knicks are, and always will be, Jalen Brunson's team. Through the first month of the 2026-27 NBA season, though — and, really, since the start of last postseason — you can make a legitimate case that Towns has been their best all-around player. And, if you're feeling spicy, maybe the best player in the entire conference.

    Recent findings suggest that that's debatable, of course. Reasonable people can forward a number of names: Giannis Antetokounmpo, off to a scorching start to his tenure in South Beach; Cade Cunningham, still the straw that stirs the drink in Detroit; Tyrese Maxey, who's been the best player on the conference's No. 1 seed in Philly; Jayson Tatum, who had Boston off to a roaring start before some slippage out West.

    Dig into the numbers, though, and Towns — the two-way heartbeat of a team that has won 11 of its past 14 games since an 0-3 start to move into a tie for second place in the East, boasting the NBA's third-best net rating in that span — has as good a case as any of them.

    Industry observers note that entering Tuesday's action, Towns ranks third in the NBA in ESPN's net points per 100 possessions, behind only Wembanyama and Dončić. He's fourth in win shares, behind only Wembanyama, Dončić and Houston Rockets center Alperen Şengün. He's fifth in The BBall Index's LEBRON and box plus-minus, and sixth in win shares per 48 minutes, value over replacement player, Neil Paine's wins above replacement and Mike Beuoy's win probability added. He's seventh in player efficiency rating, ninth in DARKO daily plus-minus and tied for 10th among healthy players in Jeremias Engelmann's xRAPM. Which is to say: Take your pick of impact metrics, and KAT's right near the top, rubbing shoulders with the best of the best.

    Sources indicate that maybe you're not such a big fan of the all-in-one alphabet-soup metrics; maybe you like your numbers a little less advanced. Well, how's this:.

    Towns enters Wednesday's 2026 Emirates NBA Cup meeting with the rival Cleveland Cavaliers averaging 21.8 points, 13.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 32.6 minutes per game. That makes him one of only three players in the NBA this season averaging at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and four dimes a night, alongside Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić. He's hitting those numbers more efficiently than ever, too, shooting 61% on 2-pointers and 42% from long distance, scoring under 1.32 points per shot attempt with a .650 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy) — both career highs.

    (Bruno Rouby/Yahoo Sports Illustration).

    Scoring plus rebounding plus playmaking plus efficiency is a pretty damn good combination. Prior to this season, Stathead's database lists only two players who've ever averaged more than 20 points per game, grabbed more than 20% of available rebounds, dished assists on more than 20% of his teammates' baskets, and posted a true shooting percentage north of .600: Giannis, back in 2019-20, and Jokić, who did it in 2021-22, '22-23 and '25-26.

    Those seasons resulted in two MVP trophies and two runner-up finishes. That's the tech giant that KAT's keeping this season.

    (For the record: Wemby and Giannis are also keeping that organization this season. Whew.).

    Much of this stellar start goes back to those five principles — pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass — that Brown's been hammering ever since he got to Newly introduced York. Towns might not be the first person you think of when you hear the word "pace," and the Knicks probably wouldn't be the first team to come to mind: They rank dead last in the NBA in number of possessions per 48 minutes, and tied for 28th in the average length of their offensive possessions. (Much, at times, to Brown's chagrin.) But while nobody will confuse Brown's charges for the Seven Seconds or Less Suns, they do move more swiftly with the 7-footer involved: The Knicks' average offensive possession is 1.3 seconds faster with Towns on the floor than off it — the largest differential of any Knick who's played actual minutes.

    "Space," obviously, is a little easier to square here. Long heralded as perhaps the sweetest-shooting significant man of all time (including, um, by himself), Towns is attempting eight 3-pointers per 100 possessions this season, the most since his last season in Minnesota and the fourth-most of his career. He boasts the third-highest average gravity of any center — an NBA Advanced Stats metric aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — behind only Wembanyama and Joel Embiid. (Towns also outpaces both in perimeter gravity when he's off the ball, meaning he's drawing more attention than either of them when he's spaced and doesn't have possession — creating wider driving and passing lanes for his teammates to exploit.).

    In a recent development, when Towns does have the ball, he's wasting precious little time before attacking. Among 80 players averaging at least 50 touches per game this season, Towns averages the second-fewest dribbles per touch and has the seventh-lowest average touch time, holding on to the ball for just 1.8 seconds on average, according to Second Spectrum tracking data. He's one of 12 Knicks under two seconds per touch — evidence of widespread adherence to Brown's insistence on quick decision-making.

    Industry observers note that when the big fella decides to move, he's often aimed at the lane. Despite spending a significant share of his floor time setting high ball screens, spacing the floor or facilitating from up top, Towns leads the Knicks in paint touches per game — he's 26th in the league in total paint touches — and is taking a career-high 53% of his shots at the rim this season.

    It has been revealed that he's actually driving to the cup less frequently — just 5.5 dribble-drives per game this season, down from 8.1 last season and 11.3 in 2024-25. He's been an absolute monster on those forays to the basket, though, scoring nearly a point per drive and shooting 67% on those plays. He's finishing tough through the contact he draws in the lane, too: Nearly 35% of the shooting fouls he absorbs have ended in an and-one — also near a career-high.

    Thanks partly to the pressure Towns puts on the rim himself, and partly to how his presence on the perimeter opens up the floor for his teammates, the Knicks take 34.5% of their field-goal attempts at the rim with him in the game — a near-top-five rate in the league, according to Cleaning the Glass. That rate drops to 25.8% when he's off the floor, which would sit just 26th in the NBA.

    That just leaves "crash the glass" … which Towns is doing to the tune of hauling in a career-high 11.3% of available offensive rebounds. He's turning the garbage into gold, too, tied for sixth in the NBA in second-chance points per game — one big reason why Latest York ranks in the top five in putback scoring efficiency.

    In a recent development, when Brown took over, he made it clear exactly what he wanted his players to do — what he believed they had to do to reach the grandest goal in the game. After achieving it, he demanded nothing less. More than any other player in orange and blue, Towns has delivered it, night after night after night.

    It has been revealed that "Ever since I got here, all I've ever remarked is that I want to do whatever it takes to win a title," Towns told reporters earlier this month. "You win one and, you know, this year I want to do it again. I'm always willing to do whatever it takes. I've always sacrificed for the betterment of the team.".

    That's the funny thing about basketball, though. Sometimes, being willing to give it up means you wind up getting it back in an even better position to do something with it.

    In a recent development, the sacrifice-minded Towns' usage rate, average time of possession and field goal attempts per 100 possessions are all up a tick from last season. And with New York more frequently operating its offense through Towns as a playmaking hub at the top of the floor — a carryover from the success the Knicks found with those looks last postseason, which has helped unlock Brunson as an off-ball weapon and unleashed a devastating split-cut game — he's averaging 43.4 frontcourt touches per game this season, according to Second Spectrum tracking. That's the fifth-highest mark in the NBA this season, and KAT's heaviest half-court workload in five years.

    Industry observers note that towns has been brilliant in that more central role, whether looking for his own opportunities or quarterbacking the offense to set the table for Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Hart and the rest of the defending champs. He has notched the assist on 21.9% of his teammates' baskets during his time on the court — a significant leap from his first two seasons as a Knick, and a near-top-10 mark among power forward/center types thus far this season.

    Fresh York's live-ball turnover rate drops by eight percentage points in KAT's minutes, and its shooting efficiency improves by eight percentage points, according to PBP Stats. When he's on the floor, nearly 60% of the Knicks' 2-point field goals have come via assist — up from 50% when he's on the bench. That's the difference between top-three in the league and bottom-five.

    "They've done a great job of making their offense multifaceted," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch told reporters when the Knicks visited — and beat — Minnesota last week. "They still have Brunson doing his thing. And now KAT, playing through him — we talked about how that was something that they found last year to go to late in the season, in the playoffs. And now, the Brunson-KAT two-man game is better than it's ever been.".

    So, too, is Towns' work on the defensive end — so often maligned over the course of his 12-year career, but something that started to become a legitimate strength early last season, sustained at a high level through the Knicks' championship run, and has carried over to the start of this season.

    Industry observers note that as aggressively as Towns crashes the offensive glass, he has hit the boards even harder on the other end, leading the NBA in defensive rebounds and total rebounds per game. All that possession-finishing has led to him finishing all 16 games he's played this season with a double-double — the longest such streak to open a season by any Knicks player ever, and the fourth-longest season-starting streak by any player since the ABA-NBA merger, according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes. KAT's tech giant there, again: Jokić, Giannis … and prime Bill Walton.

    Towns' defensive contributions extend beyond rebounding, though. He's become much more comfortable playing multiple defensive schemes, including more frequently playing up higher on the floor to take away ball-handlers' airspace in the pick-and-roll. He's been active and aggressive with his hands, posting the highest steal rate of his career and his highest block rate since 2021-22 — and, crucially, doing so without hacking, averaging his fewest personal fouls per 36 minutes since 2019-20.

    "KAT's got tremendous feel," Brown recently told reporters. "He's a smart, smart dude when it comes to a lot of things, but especially when it comes to the game of basketball.".

    And when he's sunk back into the paint in drop coverage, Towns has proved a sturdier interior deterrent than his reputation would suggest. The share of opponents' field goal attempts that come at the basket plummets with him in the game, and opponents are shooting 55.3% at the rim when he's the nearest defender, according to Second Spectrum tracking — that's 25th among 86 players who've defended at least 40 up-close attempts, and on pace to be the second-best mark of his career. All told, the Knicks are allowing just 106.3 points-per-100 in Towns' minutes — a level of defensive efficiency that would be No. 2 in the NBA, behind only his old pals in Minnesota.

    Sources indicate that so: What do you get when you combine a skeleton-key stretch big man who unlocks a championship-level offense with a defensive anchor capable of serving as the backstop of a top-five defense, all while playing major minutes at an elite level of offensive efficiency? It sure sounds like one of the best, most crucial — dare we say, most valuable? — players you can have in the modern NBA.

    Maybe, in a world where Wemby and Luka and SGA exist, that all doesn't add up to an MVP trophy. It does, though, produce a player that's a hell of a lot closer to top-five in the world than he is to missing the All-NBA ballot — which Towns did last season (unjustly, in my view). And, if KAT and the Knicks can keep up the flow they've found since their slow start, it ought to produce one hell of a title defense.

    Berkshire Hit a Record High While AI Power Stocks Sold Off. Here’s What That Says About Where Energy Money Is Going.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:42PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
    • In a recent development, over the past three months, Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.73%)(BRKB +0.85%) is up roughly 15% as of this writing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:42PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    In a recent development, over the past three months, Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.73%)(BRKB +0.85%) is up roughly 15% as of this writing. By comparison, Bloom Energy (BE -6.98%) and Caterpillar (CAT -1.17%), both headline-grabbing artificial intelligence (AI) energy plays, are down 29% and 38%, respectively. Investors aren't giving up on the companies that provide energy for AI, but they may be shifting toward more conservative investments. Here's what you need to know.

    Artificial intelligence is really just a fancy computer program. Without electricity, it can't exist. But AI uses a tremendous amount of power, resulting in consumer backlash against the data centers that host it. This is why investors have been so attracted to Bloom Energy and Caterpillar.

    Bloom Energy makes hydrogen fuel cells. These factory-produced items can be placed wherever they are needed to provide off-grid power. Caterpillar, while best known for its heavy earth-moving equipment, also makes generators that provide off-grid power. However, given the backlash against AI, investor enthusiasm for AI stocks has diminished, and these stocks have fallen alongside the broader AI trade despite still-high expectations for power demand.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile, Berkshire Hathaway's shares have been on the rise. That is at least partly a flight-to-safety trade. Berkshire Hathaway is a giant conglomerate with businesses ranging from insurance to homebuilding, and much in between. It also has more than $370 billion in cash sitting on its balance sheet to cushion it against a market downturn. That cash also provides it with the ability to buy if a bear market opens up attractive investment opportunities.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    According to recent reports, that's a good start, but there's another small wrinkle here. Over the last three months, Southern Organization (SO +1.07%), a large regulated U.S. utility, is up nearly 5%, and Kinder Morgan (KMI +1.67%), a large North American pipeline operator, is down just 2%. These businesses will both be integral to powering AI. They aren't as exciting as Bloom Energy or Cat, but that's the point right now. Investors are looking for a safe haven as AI enthusiasm hits a road bump and are shifting toward boring, reliable businesses.

    Notably, Southern offers a reliable 3.2% dividend yield, while Kinder Morgan's yield is 3.9%. Berkshire Hathaway doesn't pay a dividend; however, two of its largest divisions are its utility and energy segments. Add that to the rest of the organization's owned business portfolio and its large collection of publicly traded stocks, and you have diversification along with continued exposure to the growing demand for electricity. This is not a small matter, given that electricity demand increased by 10% between 2005 and 2025 and is projected to grow by 60% between 2025 and 2045.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    Basically, Berkshire Hathaway could offer the best of both worlds. You own a diversified and financially strong organization that is prepared to take advantage of a bear market. And you continue to have exposure to AI's growing appetite for power. All in one investment. Investors may not be dumping AI power companies; they may just be getting more selective and conservative.

    The caveat here is that Berkshire Hathaway is now trading near all-time highs. However, the tech giant has been buying back its own stock over the last two quarters, which it has historically done only when it believes the stock is trading below its intrinsic value. While it probably isn't fair to suggest Berkshire Hathaway is a deep-value opportunity, if you are looking for a safer way to play long-term energy demand from AI, the company itself thinks its stock is attractive. It's probably worth a deep dive, even if you only end up putting it on your wish list.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    It has been revealed that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Industry observers note that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.
